messages:
Maya: Heads-up — we have a customer (acme-ml) escalated for sudden p99 spikes on the chat-generation API after last runtime push. p95 up ~30% and p99 ~2x since the 3617899000 deploy. Charts: https://redwood/internal/metrics/abcde :grimacing:
Chris: thx, can you paste the model + route and any quick traces?
Maya: model: gpt-open-13b-quant, route: /v1/chat/generate, region: us-west-2. Typical seq length median 128, but p99 seq length ~512. No error rate increase, only latency.
Jamie: I remember a canary noise earlier — we flipped an SDPA compile flag to favor SDPA kernels for long sequences. Could be misselection when batch has mixed lengths.
Alex: confirmed — sdpa_fastpath=true was enabled in the build that rolled at 3617899000. It biases kernel selector toward SDPA for a wider range of seq lengths.
Maya: customer repro (curl):
```bash
curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-open-13b-quant","input":"<~500 token prompt>"}' \
  https://api.redwood.io/v1/chat/generate
```
Maya: from their trace: p99 went 1.3s -> 2.9s after the deploy. GPU util ~40-60%, token throughput drops during spikes. KV cache hit rate unchanged.
Chris: working hypothesis: SDPA path introduces micro-stalls under mixed-length batching which blow up tail latency. Two quick mitigations: (A) force kernel override to FlashAttention fallback for that model shard, (B) revert sdpa_fastpath compile flag in the runtime build.
Jamie: I can push a runtime hotpatch to allow per-model kernel_override env — low-risk. Recommend canary to 10% traffic for the affected shard first.
Infra-bot: incident created: INC-2026-042 (latency-regression-sdpa). Assigned: eng-runtime oncall.
SRE-Oncall: repro steps (local): use runtimesim replay: `runtimesim replay --trace acme-ml-2026-03-16.json --kernel=sdpa` to reproduce p99. Then `--kernel=flash` to compare. Keep batch mix the same as customer trace.
Alex: quick API to flip kernel for a model (internal):
```
PATCH /runtime/models/gpt-open-13b-quant/kernel
{ "kernel_override": "flash" }
```
Maya: applied kernel_override=flash on the customer shard at 14:42 PT, monitoring now.
Chris: will watch per-token tail and throughput. If flash helps, plan to revert sdpa_fastpath and add a stricter heuristic: require >70% of tokens in batch >256 to pick SDPA.
Maya: update — after override p99 for that shard dropped from 2.9s -> 1.4s within ~3 minutes. Customer reports improved latency. :tada:
Jamie: next steps (postmortem items): 1) add seq-length threshold to kernel selector, 2) add canary gate for compile flags, 3) add automated perf tests with mixed-length batching, 4) document runtime knobs and emergency rollback playbook.
Maya: customer asked for ETA on permanent fix and confirmation no billing impact. Billing unaffected, no errors seen.
Chris: tentative timeline: patch + unit/integration perf runs by EOD tomorrow, full rollout gated by canary results.
Alex: pinging @Product for comms to customer.
Product: acknowledged, will coordinate customer update and adjust support messaging.
Maya: thanks everyone — keeping the thread open until PRs merge and we have a rollout plan. :white_check_mark:
